images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of the MetaKernelBench pipeline.Left:one DSL-neutral specification yields paired CuTe DSL and TIRx variants.Middle:solo attempts use verifier feedback to optimize implementations and distill findings into natural-language skills.Right:only the source skill crosses to a fresh attempt in the other DSL, and paired lift compares its implementation with the solo attempt’s.

Figure 2:Construction and composition of the MetaKernelBench problem set.Left:manual screening of fused subgraphs from four upstream sources yields 74 fixed-workload problems.Right:six families show problem counts, representative computation patterns, and numerical formats.

Figure 5:Skill content across transfer outcomes.
Cells show a label’s prevalence in helped comparisons minus that in harmed comparisons, in percentage points averaged over the two directions.
Percentages under category names give each label’s prevalence over all 841 labeled skills.

Figure 6:Two GLM-5.3 transfers from passing source implementations.Top:CuTe DSL to TIRx on p68, helped, reusing a thread mapping and a diagnostic control.Bottom:TIRx to CuTe DSL on p71, harmed, retaining an eager recurrence.
Tags mark whether a graded source submission supports each claim, and runtimes are unclipped end-to-end times against solo.

Figure 8:The task instruction.
The top row summarizes the template’s parameters, and the cards quote excerpts from its sections in order, with ellipses marking omitted text.
